The central API is `fn accept<C: Callback>(callback: C) -> Result<(), HandshakeError<ServerHandshake<S, C>>>`. The next statement, `accept(callback);`, uses the inner closure as the generic argument `C` to another invocation of `accept`. Therefore the compiler must determine whether the inner closure satisfies `Callback`, i.e. whether it implements `FnOnce(&Request, Response) -> Result<Response>`.

The inner closure body is just `todo!()`. Since `todo!()` has the never type `!`, it can coerce to any return type. No runtime path is expected to execute because every operational function body uses `todo!()`. Therefore a reproducer failure would almost certainly be a compiler crash, ICE, inference failure, or incorrect trait solving/type normalization issue rather than a logical program bug.
